chunks.section: Item 4. Advisory Business > 4.1 Firm History and Ownership
chunks.text: Tennick Arlow Wealth Partners, LLC is a Virginia limited liability company formed in March 2009 by Margaret L. Tennick and Daniel R. Arlow. The Firm registered with the SEC as an investment adviser in 2011, after operating for two years as an investment adviser registered with the Virginia Division of Securities and Retail Franchising. Ms. Tennick is the Firm's Managing Partner and Chief Executive Officer, and Mr. Arlow is its Chief Investment Officer. Ms. Tennick owns 46% of the Firm's membership interests and Mr. Arlow owns 34%. The remaining 20% is held by Tennick Arlow Employee Holdings, LLC, an entity owned by nine senior employees of the Firm, none of whom holds an indirect interest of 5% or more. The Firm is managed by a Management Committee consisting of the Managing Partner, the Chief Investment Officer, the Chief Operating Officer and the Chief Financial Officer.

chunks.section: Item 4. Advisory Business > 4.2 Wealth Management Services
chunks.text: We provide continuous and regular supervisory and management services to high-net-worth individuals and families through separately managed accounts held in each client's name at an unaffiliated qualified custodian. We do not pool client assets. The client's wealth advisor gathers information about the household's assets and liabilities, cash flow requirements, tax position, estate plan, time horizon and tolerance for risk, and we document the resulting objectives, asset allocation targets and restrictions in a written Investment Policy Statement that the client signs. We construct each portfolio using the strategies described in Item 4.3 and monitor and rebalance it as described in Item 13. The service includes tax-aware implementation, including tax-loss harvesting and asset location, coordination with the client's accountant and estate attorney, and ongoing financial planning. Investment decisions for our model strategies are made by our Investment Policy Committee, which is chaired by Mr. Arlow and meets monthly, and wealth advisors implement those decisions subject to each client's Investment Policy Statement.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 4. Advisory Business > 4.3 Investment Strategies Offered
chunks.text: We manage client portfolios using the following strategies, alone or in combination: - **Core Equity.** A portfolio of 40 to 55 common stocks of U.S. large- and mid-capitalization companies selected through fundamental research. - **Dividend Growth Equity.** A portfolio of 35 to 50 companies with a record of increasing their dividends and the balance sheet capacity to continue doing so. - **Tax-Managed Municipal.** Laddered portfolios of investment-grade municipal bonds, generally rated A or better at purchase, with maturities of one to fifteen years, which may emphasize issuers in the client's state of residence. - **Taxable Fixed Income.** Portfolios of U.S. Treasury and agency securities, investment-grade corporate bonds and brokered certificates of deposit. - **Global Allocation Models.** Diversified portfolios of exchange-traded funds and mutual funds offered in five risk profiles: Conservative, Moderate Conservative, Moderate, Moderate Growth and Growth. - **Private Market Access.** For clients who are accredited investors or qualified purchasers, recommendations of unaffiliated private equity, private credit and private real estate funds, as described in Item 10.4.

chunks.section: Item 5. Fees and Compensation > 5.1 Wealth Management Fee Schedule
chunks.text: Wealth management clients pay an annual asset-based fee calculated on a tiered basis and applied to the aggregate assets of the household under our management, as follows: | Household assets under management | Annual fee rate | |---|---| | First $1,000,000 | 1.00% | | Next $2,000,000 (over $1,000,000 up to $3,000,000) | 0.80% | | Next $2,000,000 (over $3,000,000 up to $5,000,000) | 0.65% | | Next $5,000,000 (over $5,000,000 up to $10,000,000) | 0.50% | | Over $10,000,000 | 0.35% | Because the schedule is tiered, each rate applies only to the assets within its tier. For example, a household with $4,000,000 of assets under management pays an annual fee of $32,500: 1.00% on the first $1,000,000 ($10,000), 0.80% on the next $2,000,000 ($16,000) and 0.65% on the remaining $1,000,000 ($6,500). The annual fee is allocated among the household's accounts in proportion to their values unless the client instructs us to bill a single account.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 5. Fees and Compensation > 5.2 Billing Method
chunks.text: Fees are billed quarterly in advance, based on the market value of the assets in each account on the last business day of the preceding calendar quarter. Market values are the values reported by the custodian or, for assets the custodian does not price and for private fund interests and other assets without observable market prices, the values determined under our Valuation Policy. Unless a client elects to be invoiced, the client authorizes the custodian in the advisory agreement to deduct our fee directly from the account, and the deduction appears on the custodian's statement. The fee for the first partial quarter is calculated pro rata from the date the account is funded. Additions or withdrawals of $100,000 or more in a single transaction during a quarter result in a pro rata charge or credit on the next quarterly invoice. Smaller flows are not adjusted.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 5. Fees and Compensation > 5.3 Household Aggregation
chunks.text: For purposes of applying the fee schedule, we aggregate the accounts of a household, which includes the client, the client's spouse or domestic partner, their dependent children, and trusts, foundations and entities of which one or more of them is the grantor, primary beneficiary or controlling owner. Aggregation lowers the blended fee rate. It is the client's responsibility to tell us about related accounts that may qualify for aggregation. Assets in a Fixed Income Mandate are billed under the Fixed Income Mandate schedule and are not included in the household total used to apply the wealth management schedule.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 5. Fees and Compensation > 5.4 Minimums and Negotiability
chunks.text: The minimum annual fee for a wealth management household is $10,000. The Managing Partner may waive or reduce the account minimum and the minimum annual fee, for example for family members of existing clients. Our fees are negotiable. Households that became clients under earlier fee schedules and employees of the Firm may pay different fees, and comparable services may be available from other advisers at lower cost.

chunks.section: Item 5. Fees and Compensation > 5.5 Fixed Income Mandates and Financial Planning Fees
chunks.text: Clients who engage us to manage a standalone Tax-Managed Municipal or Taxable Fixed Income portfolio (a "Fixed Income Mandate") pay 0.40% annually on the first $5,000,000 and 0.30% on assets above $5,000,000. The minimum Fixed Income Mandate is $2,000,000. Standalone financial planning engagements are charged a fixed fee between $5,000 and $25,000, depending on the complexity of the client's circumstances and the scope of the engagement; 50% of the fee is due when the engagement letter is signed and the balance is due when the written plan is delivered. Hourly consulting is charged at $400 per hour.

chunks.section: Item 5. Fees and Compensation > 5.6 Other Fees and Expenses
chunks.text: Clients bear separately the charges imposed by custodians and other third parties, including transaction charges on certain trades, dealer markups and markdowns on fixed income trades, wire and transfer fees, and account termination fees. Mutual funds, exchange-traded funds and private funds charge management fees and other expenses, disclosed in their offering documents, that clients bear indirectly in addition to our fee. Uninvested cash is held in the custodian's sweep program, on which the custodian earns compensation. We receive no portion of any of these fees or of any sweep program compensation.

chunks.section: Item 5. Fees and Compensation > 5.7 Termination and Refunds
chunks.text: Either party may terminate the advisory agreement upon 30 days' written notice. Prepaid fees are refunded on a pro rata basis for the number of days remaining in the quarter after the effective date of termination, and refunds are paid within 15 business days. A client who terminates within five business days of signing the advisory agreement receives a full refund of any fees paid. For standalone planning engagements terminated before delivery of the plan, we refund any portion of the fee paid that exceeds the value of the work performed to the termination date.

chunks.section: Item 8. Methods of Analysis, Investment Strategies and Risk of Loss > 8.1 Methods of Analysis
chunks.text: For individual equity securities, we use fundamental analysis of a company's financial statements, earnings quality, competitive position, management, capital allocation and valuation. For fixed income securities, we use credit analysis, which for municipal bonds includes the issuer's revenue base, debt service coverage and call provisions. For funds, we evaluate the manager's process, organization, fees, liquidity terms and operational controls. We set strategic asset allocations using capital market assumptions that the Investment Policy Committee reviews at least annually. Our sources include company filings, credit rating agency reports, third-party research, offering documents and the financial press.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 8. Methods of Analysis, Investment Strategies and Risk of Loss > 8.2 Investment Strategies
chunks.text: Our approach is long-term. We construct portfolios around strategic asset allocation targets set in each Investment Policy Statement, and the Investment Policy Committee may tilt model allocations by up to three percentage points relative to those targets when it believes valuations warrant. We generally hold individual securities for several years, but we may sell a position within a shorter period when our assessment changes, to harvest a loss, or to raise cash. We do not use margin, sell securities short or write uncovered options in client accounts, although we may write covered call options against concentrated positions at a client's request.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 8. Methods of Analysis, Investment Strategies and Risk of Loss > 8.3 General Risk of Loss
chunks.text: Investing in securities involves risk of loss that clients should be prepared to bear. We do not guarantee the performance of any account or the achievement of any objective, and past performance is not indicative of future results. The following risks are the principal risks of our strategies; not every risk applies to every account.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 8. Methods of Analysis, Investment Strategies and Risk of Loss > 8.4 Principal Risks
chunks.text: **Market risk.** The value of securities may decline because of general market conditions, changes in interest rates or inflation, economic or political developments, or investor sentiment, which may affect an entire market or sector regardless of the merits of an individual issuer. **Equity securities and concentration risk.** Common stocks are subordinate to an issuer's debt and may lose value rapidly. The Core Equity and Dividend Growth Equity strategies hold a limited number of positions, and an account that holds a concentrated legacy position may be more volatile than a diversified portfolio. **Interest rate and call risk.** The value of fixed income securities generally falls when interest rates rise, and longer maturities are more sensitive. Issuers of callable bonds may redeem them before maturity when rates fall, and the proceeds may be reinvested at lower yields. **Credit risk.** An issuer may fail to pay interest or principal when due, or its credit rating may be lowered, reducing the value of its securities. **Municipal securities risk.** Municipal bonds may be affected by the financial condition of the issuing state or locality, changes in tax laws that reduce the value of tax exemption, and legislative or political developments. Portfolios that emphasize a single state are more exposed to that state's economy and fiscal position. **Liquidity risk.** Some securities, including certain municipal bonds, brokered certificates of deposit and all private fund interests, trade infrequently or not at all, and may be sold only at a discount or after a delay. **Fund risk.** Exchange-traded funds and mutual funds are subject to the risks of their underlying holdings and to their own fees, and exchange-traded funds may trade at a premium or discount to net asset

chunks.section: Item 10. Other Financial Industry Activities and Affiliations > 10.2 Kilnwick Tax Services, LLC
chunks.text: Kilnwick Tax Services, LLC ("Kilnwick") is a tax preparation and tax planning firm under common control with the Firm: Ms. Tennick and Mr. Arlow together own all of Kilnwick's membership interests. Kilnwick prepares federal and state income tax returns and gift tax returns for individuals and trusts, including some of our clients. Kilnwick's fees are charged separately under a written engagement letter and are not offset against our advisory fees. Because Ms. Tennick and Mr. Arlow benefit from Kilnwick's revenue, we have an incentive to recommend Kilnwick to our clients. We address this conflict by disclosing it, by not requiring any client to use Kilnwick, by paying our wealth advisors no compensation for referrals to Kilnwick, and by sharing client information with Kilnwick only with the client's written consent.

chunks.text: We recommend unaffiliated private funds to eligible clients. We do not sponsor or serve as general partner of any private fund and receive no compensation from any fund sponsor. chunks.section: Item 11. Code of Ethics, Participation or Interest in Client Transactions and Personal Trading > 11.1 Code of Ethics
chunks.text: We have adopted a Code of Ethics under Rule 204A-1 under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 (the "Advisers Act"). The Code sets standards of business conduct that reflect our fiduciary duty and governs personal trading, gifts and entertainment, political contributions, outside business activities and material nonpublic information. The Firm treats all of its employees as access persons. We will provide a copy of the Code to any client or prospective client on request.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 11. Code of Ethics, Participation or Interest in Client Transactions and Personal Trading > 11.2 Personal Trading
chunks.text: Our employees may buy or sell for their own accounts the same securities that we buy or sell for clients. To address the conflicts this creates, the Code requires employees to obtain pre-clearance before trading most reportable securities, prohibits trading during blackout periods around trades in our model strategies, prohibits participation in initial public offerings, requires prior approval for investments in private placements, and requires employees to submit quarterly transaction reports and annual holdings reports, which our compliance staff review.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 11. Code of Ethics, Participation or Interest in Client Transactions and Personal Trading > 11.3 Participation or Interest in Client Transactions
chunks.text: Employee accounts may be included in aggregated orders with client accounts, in which case they receive the same average price and bear the same transaction costs as participating client accounts. We do not effect principal transactions or agency cross transactions for client accounts, and we do not recommend to clients securities in which the Firm or any related person has a material financial interest.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 12. Brokerage Practices > 12.1 Selection and Recommendation of Custodians
chunks.text: We require clients to maintain their accounts with a qualified custodian that we recommend. We recommend Harlowe Crest Securities, LLC, a registered broker-dealer and member of FINRA and SIPC, for most accounts, and Brindlemoor Trust Company, N.A., a national trust bank, for trust accounts and certain retirement accounts. We are not affiliated with either custodian. In recommending a custodian we consider the quality and cost of its execution, its custody and reporting capabilities, its technology, its client service and its financial strength. The custodian executes most trades for accounts it holds, and clients may pay more for a transaction than they would pay elsewhere.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 12. Brokerage Practices > 12.2 Research and Other Soft Dollar Benefits
chunks.text: We have no soft dollar arrangements. Our custodians make available to us, without charge or at a discount, services that benefit us but not any particular client, including trading and rebalancing software, electronic account data, access to institutional share classes, research and educational conferences. These benefits are not conditioned on any volume of business, but they give us an incentive to recommend a custodian for our own benefit rather than for our clients' interest in favorable execution. We address this conflict through the best execution review described in Item 12.5.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 12. Brokerage Practices > 12.3 Brokerage for Client Referrals
chunks.text: We do not select or recommend broker-dealers or custodians on the basis of client referrals.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 12. Brokerage Practices > 12.4 Directed Brokerage
chunks.text: We generally do not permit clients to direct us to use a broker-dealer other than our recommended custodians. If we agree to a client's direction, we may be unable to negotiate commissions, obtain volume discounts or achieve best execution, and the client's orders may be placed after aggregated orders for other clients.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 12. Brokerage Practices > 12.5 Aggregation and Allocation of Trades
chunks.text: When we buy or sell the same security for more than one account, we may aggregate the orders into a block trade if we believe aggregation is consistent with our duty to seek best execution. Each participating account receives the average price for the block and bears its proportionate share of any transaction costs. The allocation of each block is determined before the order is placed. A partially filled order is allocated pro rata based on the intended allocation. Because client accounts are held at two custodians, we sequence model trades between custodians using a rotation designed so that neither custodian's clients are consistently traded first. Our Best Execution Committee regularly reviews execution quality, custodian services and the costs borne by clients.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 12. Brokerage Practices > 12.6 Trade Errors
chunks.text: When we cause a trade error in a client account, we correct it promptly so that the client is restored to the position it would have occupied had the error not occurred. The Firm reimburses the client for any resulting loss, and any resulting gain remains in the client's account.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 13. Review of Accounts > 13.1 Periodic Reviews
chunks.text: Each household's wealth advisor meets with the household at least annually to review its objectives, financial circumstances and Investment Policy Statement. Our portfolio management staff review every account at least quarterly for adherence to its model, its asset allocation targets and any client restrictions. An account is rebalanced when any asset class deviates from its target weight by more than five percentage points, or sooner when cash flows, tax considerations or client instructions require. Additional reviews are triggered by significant deposits or withdrawals, changes in a client's circumstances reported to us, and changes in a model strategy. The Chief Investment Officer oversees the review process.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 13. Review of Accounts > 13.2 Client Reports
chunks.text: Clients receive account statements directly from their custodian at least quarterly. We send each client a quarterly report showing holdings, asset allocation, performance net of fees and the calculation of the fee billed, and an annual report of realized gains and losses. We urge clients to compare our reports with their custodian's statements.

chunks.section: Item 14. Client Referrals and Other Compensation > 14.1 Economic Benefits from Custodians
chunks.text: As described in Item 12.2, we receive economic benefits from our custodians in the form of services and support. Our custodians may also pay a portion of the cost of educational events that we host for clients. These benefits create a conflict of interest that we address as described in Item 12.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 14. Client Referrals and Other Compensation > 14.2 Compensation for Client Referrals
chunks.text: We do not directly or indirectly compensate any person for client referrals, and we do not participate in any custodian referral program. Clients who refer friends or family members to us receive no compensation or fee reduction for doing so.

chunks.section: Item 15. Custody > 15.1 Deduction of Advisory Fees
chunks.text: We have custody of client assets because clients authorize us to deduct our fees directly from their accounts. Client assets are held by the qualified custodians described in Item 12, which send account statements directly to clients at least quarterly. Clients should review those statements carefully and compare them with the reports we provide.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 15. Custody > 15.2 Standing Letters of Authorization
chunks.text: Some clients execute standing letters of authorization with their custodian that permit us to direct transfers from their accounts to third parties they designate. We treat these arrangements as custody and comply with the conditions described by the SEC staff: the client's written instruction to the custodian names the recipient, the client may revoke it at any time, the custodian notifies the client after each transfer, we cannot change the recipient, and the recipient is not related to the Firm. Assets subject to these arrangements are not included in the surprise examination described below.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 15. Custody > 15.3 Trustee Appointments and Surprise Examination
chunks.text: Because Ms. Tennick and two other supervised persons serve as trustees of certain client trusts, the Firm is deemed to have custody of those trusts' assets. As required by Rule 206(4)-2 under the Advisers Act, those assets are subject to an annual surprise examination by an independent public accountant, Pemberline & Rusk LLP, at a time chosen by the accountant without prior notice to the Firm. The accountant files Form ADV-E with the SEC within 120 days of the examination date. The trusts' assets are held by Brindlemoor Trust Company, N.A. or Harlowe Crest Securities, LLC, which send statements to the trust beneficiaries or their representatives as well as to the trustees.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 16. Investment Discretion > 16.1 Discretionary and Non-Discretionary Authority
chunks.text: Most clients grant us discretionary authority in the advisory agreement to determine, without obtaining consent for each transaction, the securities to be bought and sold and the amounts, subject to the client's Investment Policy Statement and any restrictions the client has imposed. This authority is a limited power of attorney: it does not permit us to withdraw assets from an account, except for the deduction of our fees and transfers under a standing letter of authorization. For non-discretionary accounts, we obtain the client's approval before each transaction, and the client's account may therefore be traded after discretionary accounts, at a different price.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 17. Voting Client Securities > 17.1 Proxy Voting Authority and Policy
chunks.text: Unless a client retains proxy voting authority in the advisory agreement, we vote proxies for the securities in the client's accounts under our Proxy Voting Policy, in what we believe to be the client's best interest, generally supporting management on routine matters and evaluating other proposals case by case against our voting guidelines. If a vote presents a conflict of interest, the Chief Compliance Officer reviews the matter and the vote is cast according to the guidelines without discretion. A client may direct our vote on a particular solicitation by contacting the client's wealth advisor at least five business days before the meeting.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 17. Voting Client Securities > 17.2 Proxy Voting Service Provider
chunks.text: We have retained Veridane Proxy Services, Inc. to provide proxy research and vote recommendations under guidelines adopted by our Investment Policy Committee, to execute votes through its electronic platform and to maintain voting records. The Chief Compliance Officer reviews Veridane's conflicts policies, capacity and accuracy annually. Clients may obtain a copy of our Proxy Voting Policy and a record of how we voted their securities by contacting the Chief Compliance Officer.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 17. Voting Client Securities > 17.3 Class Actions and Other Legal Proceedings
chunks.text: We do not advise clients or act on their behalf in legal proceedings, including bankruptcies and class action lawsuits, involving securities held in their accounts. Custodians forward related notices to clients, and clients are responsible for deciding whether to participate.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026

chunks.text: We do not require or solicit prepayment of more than $1,200 in fees per client six months or more in advance. We have no financial condition that is reasonably likely to impair our ability to meet our contractual commitments to clients, and the Firm has not been the subject of a bankruptcy petition at any time during the past ten years.

chunks.section: Preamble
chunks.text: # Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual **Tennick Arlow Wealth Partners, LLC** **Version 7.0, effective January 15, 2026** > **SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT: FOR BENCHMARK USE ONLY.** This document is fictional. Tennick Arlow Wealth Partners, LLC, Kilnwick Tax Services, LLC and all persons, service providers and figures named herein are invented for the purpose of evaluating document-processing systems. It is not an offer to sell securities and does not describe any real entity.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. PURPOSE, SCOPE AND DEFINITIONS > 1.1 Purpose
chunks.text: This Manual sets out the written policies and procedures that Tennick Arlow Wealth Partners, LLC (the "Firm") has adopted under Rule 206(4)-7 under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 (the "Advisers Act") to prevent, detect and correct violations of the Advisers Act and the rules under it. Section 3 through Section 7 constitute the Firm's Code of Ethics under Rule 204A-1. This Manual is designed around the risks presented by the Firm's business: discretionary management of separately managed accounts for high-net-worth households, held at unaffiliated qualified custodians, together with financial planning and the recommendation of third-party private funds.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. PURPOSE, SCOPE AND DEFINITIONS > 1.2 Scope
chunks.text: This Manual applies to every Supervised Person. Temporary staff, interns and consultants who have access to client information or to the Firm's trading systems are subject to this Manual to the extent the Chief Compliance Officer designates in writing. A Supervised Person who is uncertain whether a policy applies to a particular situation must ask the CCO before acting.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. PURPOSE, SCOPE AND DEFINITIONS > 1.3 Definitions
chunks.text: "Access Person" means every Supervised Person. The Firm treats all Supervised Persons as Access Persons because all of them may have access to nonpublic information about client holdings and trading. "Beneficial Ownership" has the meaning used in Rule 16a-1(a)(2) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and includes securities held by a Supervised Person's spouse or domestic partner, minor children and other members of the household. "CCO" means the Chief Compliance Officer designated under Section 2.1. "Compliance Platform" means the compliance software provided by Kettleby Compliance Systems, Inc., through which Supervised Persons submit pre-clearance requests, reports, certifications and gift and political contribution disclosures. "Covered Account" means any account in which a Supervised Person has Beneficial Ownership and that can hold Reportable Securities. "Management Committee" means the committee consisting of the Managing Partner, the Chief Investment Officer, the Chief Operating Officer and the Chief Financial Officer. "Reportable Security" means any security as defined in Section 202(a)(18) of the Advisers Act, except direct obligations of the U.S. government, money market instruments, shares of money market funds, shares of open-end mutual funds not advised by the Firm and interests in 529 plans. "Supervised Person" means each member, officer and employee of the Firm and any other person who provides investment advice on behalf of the Firm and is subject to its supervision and control.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. PURPOSE, SCOPE AND DEFINITIONS > 1.4 Exceptions and Violations
chunks.text: Only the CCO may grant an exception to this Manual, and every exception must be in writing and recorded in the Compliance Platform. A Supervised Person who becomes aware of a violation of this Manual must report it promptly to the CCO. Violations may result in sanctions ranging from a written warning or disgorgement of profits to suspension or termination of employment.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. CHIEF COMPLIANCE OFFICER > 2.1 Designation and Reporting Line
chunks.text: The Management Committee has designated Theodora K. Marsh as the Firm's Chief Compliance Officer. The CCO reports to the Managing Partner and has direct and unrestricted access to the Management Committee. The CCO has full authority to develop and enforce the policies in this Manual, to obtain any record of the Firm and to require any Supervised Person to explain any activity.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. CHIEF COMPLIANCE OFFICER > 2.2 Responsibilities
chunks.text: The CCO administers the compliance program. The CCO's responsibilities include maintaining and updating this Manual; administering the Code of Ethics; reviewing and approving advertisements; monitoring trading, allocation and best execution; overseeing the privacy and information security programs together with the Information Security Officer; maintaining the Firm's Form ADV and delivering it to clients; conducting the annual review under Section 15; and training Supervised Persons.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. CHIEF COMPLIANCE OFFICER > 2.3 Compliance Manager and Delegation
chunks.text: Nadia Farrokh, Compliance Manager, acts for the CCO when the CCO is absent or unavailable, and may perform any task in this Manual that is assigned to the CCO, other than granting an exception under Section 1.4. The Compliance Manager reviews the CCO's own personal trading, gifts and political contributions. The CCO may delegate other tasks to members of the compliance staff, but remains responsible for the compliance program.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. CHIEF COMPLIANCE OFFICER > 2.4 Compliance Calendar and Testing
chunks.text: The CCO maintains a compliance calendar of recurring obligations, including Form ADV amendments, Form 13F and Form 13H filings, code of ethics reports, custody examinations and vendor reviews. The CCO performs forensic and transactional testing throughout the year and records the results in the Compliance Platform so that they are available for the annual review.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. CHIEF COMPLIANCE OFFICER > 2.5 Regulatory Examinations and Inquiries
chunks.text: Any Supervised Person who receives a telephone call, letter, email or visit from the SEC, a state securities regulator or any other regulatory authority must refer it immediately to the CCO and must not respond substantively. The CCO coordinates each examination, including the entrance interview, document requests and the production log, and determines with the Managing Partner whether to involve outside counsel. The CCO prepares the Firm's written response to any deficiency letter within the time requested by the staff, tracks each corrective action to completion, and retains a complete examination file.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. CODE OF ETHICS > 3.1 Standards of Business Conduct
chunks.text: The Firm is a fiduciary. Supervised Persons must place the interests of clients first, must not take advantage of their position, must avoid actual and potential conflicts of interest or disclose and manage those that cannot be avoided, and must comply with the federal securities laws. Supervised Persons may not employ any device, scheme or artifice to defraud a client or engage in any act or practice that would operate as a fraud or deceit on a client.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. CODE OF ETHICS > 3.2 Outside Business Activities
chunks.text: A Supervised Person may not serve as an officer, director, trustee, general partner or employee of any other entity, or accept compensation from any person other than the Firm, without the prior written approval of the CCO. Service as trustee of a client trust requires the approval of the CCO and is subject to the custody procedures maintained by the Operations department. A Supervised Person may not serve on the board of a public company without the approval of the Management Committee.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. CODE OF ETHICS > 3.3 Acknowledgment
chunks.text: Each Supervised Person must acknowledge in writing that he or she has received, read and will comply with the Code of Ethics within ten days of joining the Firm, within ten days of any material amendment and annually as part of the certification in Section 16.3.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. CODE OF ETHICS > 3.4 Reporting Violations
chunks.text: Supervised Persons must report any violation of the Code of Ethics promptly to the CCO. The Firm does not tolerate retaliation against any person who reports a suspected violation in good faith. Reports may be made anonymously through the Compliance Platform.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING AND PRE-CLEARANCE > 4.1 Covered Accounts
chunks.text: Each Supervised Person must disclose every Covered Account on joining the Firm and within ten days of opening a new one. Covered Accounts must be maintained at a broker-dealer or custodian that provides an electronic data feed to the Compliance Platform, unless the CCO grants a written exception.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING AND PRE-CLEARANCE > 4.2 Pre-Clearance Requirement
chunks.text: A Supervised Person must obtain pre-clearance through the Compliance Platform before buying or selling a Reportable Security in a Covered Account. Pre-clearance is not required for transactions in exchange-traded funds on the broad-based index list maintained by Compliance, transactions under an automatic investment plan, or transactions in an account over which the Supervised Person has no direct or indirect influence or control. Pre-clearance requests are approved or denied by the CCO or the Compliance Manager; requests submitted by the CCO are approved or denied by the Compliance Manager. A request will be denied if the security is on the Restricted List, if the transaction would fall within the Blackout Window in Section 4.4, or if the reviewer determines that the transaction presents a conflict with client trading.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING AND PRE-CLEARANCE > 4.3 Duration of Approval
chunks.text: A pre-clearance approval is valid only until the close of regular trading on the business day on which it is granted. An order that is not executed within that period, including an unfilled limit order, requires a new request. Good-until-cancelled orders are not permitted in Covered Accounts.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING AND PRE-CLEARANCE > 4.4 Blackout Window
chunks.text: A Supervised Person may not buy or sell a Reportable Security on any day on which a client order in that security is pending, or within three business days after the completion of a model-wide trade in that security (the "Blackout Window"). If a Supervised Person trades within the Blackout Window, the CCO may require the trade to be reversed and any profit disgorged to a charity selected by the CCO.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING AND PRE-CLEARANCE > 4.5 Minimum Holding Period
chunks.text: A Reportable Security acquired in a Covered Account must be held for at least 30 calendar days. Profits realized on a sale within 30 calendar days of purchase, measured on a last-in, first-out basis, must be disgorged to a charity selected by the CCO. The CCO may grant a written hardship exception, for example when a sale is required to meet an unforeseen personal liquidity need, and records the reason for each exception.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING AND PRE-CLEARANCE > 4.6 Initial Public Offerings and Limited Offerings
chunks.text: Supervised Persons may not acquire securities in an initial public offering. A Supervised Person may acquire securities in a limited offering, including an interest in a private fund, only with the prior written approval of the CCO, or in the case of the CCO, of the Managing Partner. In considering a request, the CCO considers whether the opportunity should be reserved for clients.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING AND PRE-CLEARANCE > 4.7 Reporting
chunks.text: Each Supervised Person must submit an initial holdings report no later than ten days after becoming a Supervised Person, with information current as of a date not more than 45 days before that date. Each Supervised Person must submit a quarterly transaction report no later than 30 days after the end of each calendar quarter, and an annual holdings report by February 14 of each year, with information current as of December 31 of the prior year. Electronic data feeds and duplicate statements received by the Compliance Platform satisfy the reporting obligation for the accounts they cover, provided the Supervised Person confirms their completeness.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING AND PRE-CLEARANCE > 4.8 Review of Personal Trading
chunks.text: The compliance staff review personal trading monthly against client trading, the Restricted List, the Blackout Window and the holding period, and document each review in the Compliance Platform. The Compliance Manager reviews the CCO's personal trading.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. GIFTS AND ENTERTAINMENT > 5.1 General Principle
chunks.text: Supervised Persons may not give or accept any gift or entertainment that could reasonably be expected to influence, or appear to influence, the recipient's judgment, and may never give or accept cash or cash equivalents, including gift cards.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. GIFTS AND ENTERTAINMENT > 5.2 Gifts
chunks.text: No Supervised Person may accept gifts with an aggregate value exceeding $250 per calendar year from any single person or entity that does business with, or seeks to do business with, the Firm, including clients, custodians, fund sponsors and vendors. The same limit applies to gifts given by a Supervised Person on behalf of the Firm. Every gift with a value above $50, given or received, must be reported in the Compliance Platform within ten business days. A gift that exceeds the limit must be returned or, if return is impractical, donated to charity at the direction of the CCO.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. GIFTS AND ENTERTAINMENT > 5.3 Business Entertainment
chunks.text: Business entertainment is permitted when the host is present and the purpose is business. Business entertainment with an estimated cost exceeding $400 per person per event requires the prior approval of the CCO. Entertainment at which the host is not present is treated as a gift under Section 5.2. Travel and lodging offered by a vendor or fund sponsor may be accepted only with the prior approval of the CCO, and the Firm generally pays its own travel costs for due diligence visits.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. GIFTS AND ENTERTAINMENT > 5.4 Union and Government Officials
chunks.text: Gifts and entertainment provided to an official of a labor union or of a union-affiliated benefit plan must be recorded so that the Firm can determine whether it must file Form LM-10 with the Department of Labor. No gift or entertainment may be offered to a government official without the prior approval of the CCO.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. POLITICAL CONTRIBUTIONS > 6.1 Background
chunks.text: Rule 206(4)-5 under the Advisers Act prohibits an adviser from receiving compensation for advisory services to a government entity for two years after the adviser or any of its covered associates makes a contribution to certain officials of that entity. The Firm does not currently advise any government entity. Because an existing client may become affiliated with a government entity, and because the Firm may seek such clients in the future, the Firm applies the following controls to all Supervised Persons.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. POLITICAL CONTRIBUTIONS > 6.2 Pre-Clearance of Contributions
chunks.text: All Supervised Persons must obtain pre-clearance from the CCO before making any political contribution, regardless of amount, to a state or local official, a candidate for state or local office, a state or local political party, or a political action committee. This requirement applies to contributions by the Supervised Person's spouse or domestic partner made from jointly held funds. Supervised Persons may not solicit or coordinate contributions for any official or candidate, and may not do indirectly anything they may not do directly. The CCO records each request and decision in the Compliance Platform.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. POLITICAL CONTRIBUTIONS > 6.3 New Hire Look-Back
chunks.text: Before an offer of employment is extended to a candidate who will solicit clients or supervise those who do, the CCO reviews the political contributions made by the candidate during the two years before the hiring date. For all other candidates, the review covers the six months before the hiring date.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. POLITICAL CONTRIBUTIONS > 6.4 Recordkeeping
chunks.text: The CCO maintains a record of the contributions of each Supervised Person, of any government entity clients and of any payments to state or local political parties or political action committees, as required by Rule 204-2(a)(18).

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. INSIDER TRADING AND MATERIAL NONPUBLIC INFORMATION > 7.1 Policy
chunks.text: No Supervised Person may trade, for a client or for any Covered Account, while in possession of material nonpublic information, or communicate material nonpublic information to anyone who does not need it for a legitimate business purpose. Information is material if a reasonable investor would consider it important to an investment decision, and nonpublic if it has not been disseminated to the investing public.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. INSIDER TRADING AND MATERIAL NONPUBLIC INFORMATION > 7.2 Sources of Information
chunks.text: Supervised Persons may receive material nonpublic information from clients who are officers, directors or large shareholders of public companies, from Kilnwick Tax Services, LLC in the course of shared engagements, from fund sponsors and from outside business activities. Supervised Persons must treat all such information as confidential.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. INSIDER TRADING AND MATERIAL NONPUBLIC INFORMATION > 7.3 Procedures on Receipt
chunks.text: A Supervised Person who believes he or she may have received material nonpublic information must stop trading in the affected securities, must not discuss the information with anyone other than the CCO, and must report it to the CCO immediately. The CCO determines whether the information is material and nonpublic and whether to add the issuer to the Restricted List.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. INSIDER TRADING AND MATERIAL NONPUBLIC INFORMATION > 7.4 Restricted List
chunks.text: The CCO maintains a Restricted List in the Compliance Platform. Issuers are placed on the Restricted List when the Firm or a Supervised Person may possess material nonpublic information about them, or when a client is an officer, director or 10% shareholder of the issuer and the Firm manages that client's holdings of the issuer's securities, including sales under Rule 144 or a Rule 10b5-1 plan. Pre-clearance requests in restricted securities are denied automatically. Client trades in a restricted security require the CCO's approval.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. MARKETING AND ADVERTISING REVIEW > 8.1 Scope
chunks.text: This Section implements Rule 206(4)-1 under the Advisers Act (the "Marketing Rule"). An advertisement includes any communication by the Firm that offers the Firm's advisory services to more than one person, including the website, social media content, pitch materials, newsletters, event presentations and performance reports distributed to prospective clients.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. MARKETING AND ADVERTISING REVIEW > 8.2 Pre-Use Approval
chunks.text: Every advertisement must be approved in writing by the CCO before its first use; in the CCO's absence the Compliance Manager may approve it. The approval, the final version of the advertisement and the support for every statement of fact in it are recorded in the Marketing Review Log. Material changes to an approved advertisement require a new approval.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. MARKETING AND ADVERTISING REVIEW > 8.3 Performance
chunks.text: Performance in an advertisement must be presented net of fees, with gross performance only alongside net performance with equal prominence, and must include one-, five- and ten-year periods ending on a date no earlier than the most recent calendar quarter-end. The Firm presents performance only for its model strategy composites. Hypothetical performance may be shown only to a prospective client who has requested it and has the resources to evaluate it, and only with the approval of the CCO. Extracted performance must be accompanied by the performance of the total portfolio.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. MARKETING AND ADVERTISING REVIEW > 8.4 Testimonials, Endorsements and Third-Party Ratings
chunks.text: The Firm does not compensate any person for testimonials, endorsements or client referrals. The use of any testimonial, endorsement or third-party rating in an advertisement requires the approval of the CCO, who confirms that the required disclosures are included and, for ratings, that the rating was not procured through payment.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. MARKETING AND ADVERTISING REVIEW > 8.5 Social Media
chunks.text: Supervised Persons may use professional networking profiles for business only in the form approved by Compliance. Business content may be posted only if it is pre-approved content from the Firm's library. Supervised Persons may not like, share or comment on third-party content about the Firm's services. Business social media activity is captured by the Firm's archiving system described in Section 14.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. TRADE AGGREGATION AND ALLOCATION > 9.1 Policy
chunks.text: No account may be favored over another in the aggregation or allocation of trades. The Head of Trading, Simone Kerrigan, is responsible for the trading desk's compliance with this Section.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. TRADE AGGREGATION AND ALLOCATION > 9.2 Aggregation
chunks.text: The trading desk may aggregate orders for the same security across accounts when doing so is consistent with the duty to seek best execution. Each account participating in an aggregated order receives the average price and bears its pro rata share of transaction costs. Covered Accounts may participate in an aggregated order on the same terms as client accounts, but may never receive a better allocation.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. TRADE AGGREGATION AND ALLOCATION > 9.3 Allocation
chunks.text: The allocation of each aggregated order is recorded in the order management system before the order is placed. A partially filled order is allocated pro rata to the participating accounts based on their intended allocations, rounded to the nearest whole share or, for fixed income securities, to the nearest $5,000 of par value. Any departure from the intended allocation must be approved by the Head of Trading and the CCO and documented with the reason.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. TRADE AGGREGATION AND ALLOCATION > 9.4 Trade Rotation Across Custodians
chunks.text: Because client accounts are held at two custodians, orders for a model-wide trade are sequenced between custodians according to a rotation that the order management system generates randomly each month. The Head of Trading may not change the rotation without the approval of the CCO.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. TRADE AGGREGATION AND ALLOCATION > 9.5 Trade Errors
chunks.text: A trade error is any error in the placement, execution or allocation of a trade, including a trade for the wrong account, security, side or quantity, or a trade that violates a client's restrictions. Trade errors are corrected promptly at no cost to the client. The Firm reimburses the client for any loss, and any gain remains in the client's account. The Head of Trading records every trade error in the Trade Error Log, and the CCO reviews each entry. Any trade error resulting in a loss or gain exceeding $5,000 is reported to the Management Committee at its next meeting.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 10. BEST EXECUTION > 10.1 Duty
chunks.text: The Firm seeks to execute client transactions so that the total cost or proceeds in each transaction is the most favorable reasonably available under the circumstances. Best execution does not require the lowest possible commission; the Firm considers price, speed, likelihood of execution and settlement, the size and type of the order and the quality of custodial services.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 10. BEST EXECUTION > 10.2 Best Execution Committee
chunks.text: The Best Execution Committee consists of the Head of Trading, who chairs it, the Chief Investment Officer, the Chief Operating Officer and the CCO. The Committee meets semi-annually. It reviews execution quality statistics from each custodian, fixed income markups and markdowns, trade-away activity, the economic benefits the Firm receives from custodians and the continued suitability of each recommended custodian, and records its conclusions in minutes.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 10. BEST EXECUTION > 10.3 Fixed Income Execution
chunks.text: For fixed income trades above $250,000 of par value, the trading desk seeks at least three competitive quotes where practicable and records the quotes received. When fewer than three quotes are available, the trader records the reason.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 11. CYBERSECURITY AND INFORMATION SECURITY > 11.1 Program
chunks.text: The Firm maintains a written information security program designed to protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of client information and the Firm's systems. The program is based on a risk assessment that the Information Security Officer updates at least annually.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 11. CYBERSECURITY AND INFORMATION SECURITY > 11.2 Information Security Officer
chunks.text: Owen Stahlberg, Director of Technology, serves as the Firm's Information Security Officer. The Information Security Officer is responsible for the program in this Section, reports on it to the Management Committee quarterly and coordinates with the CCO on matters of regulatory compliance.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 11. CYBERSECURITY AND INFORMATION SECURITY > 11.3 Access Controls
chunks.text: Multi-factor authentication is required for every system that contains client information and for all remote access. Access is granted on a least-privilege basis. The Information Security Officer reviews user access rights quarterly. Access for a departing Supervised Person is disabled no later than the end of the business day on which employment ends.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 11. CYBERSECURITY AND INFORMATION SECURITY > 11.4 Testing
chunks.text: The Firm engages Tallowmere Security Partners to conduct an external penetration test of the Firm's network and client-facing applications annually. Vulnerability scans are performed quarterly, and Supervised Persons are subject to quarterly simulated phishing exercises. Findings are tracked to remediation by the Information Security Officer.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 11. CYBERSECURITY AND INFORMATION SECURITY > 11.5 Vendor Oversight
chunks.text: The Information Security Officer and the Chief Operating Officer conduct due diligence on each vendor with access to client information before it is engaged and annually thereafter. Contracts with such vendors must require the vendor to protect client information and to notify the Firm as soon as possible, and in no event later than 72 hours, after becoming aware of a breach affecting the Firm's information.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 11. CYBERSECURITY AND INFORMATION SECURITY > 11.6 Incident Reporting and Response
chunks.text: Any Supervised Person who suspects a cybersecurity incident must report it to the Information Security Officer within one hour of discovery. The Information Security Officer activates the Incident Response Team described in Section 10 of the Business Continuity Plan. Where sensitive customer information has been, or is reasonably likely to have been, accessed or used without authorization, the Firm notifies affected individuals as soon as practicable, and in no event later than 30 days after becoming aware of the incident, as required by Regulation S-P, and makes any notifications required by state law.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 11. CYBERSECURITY AND INFORMATION SECURITY > 11.7 Cyber Insurance
chunks.text: The Firm maintains a cyber liability insurance policy. The Chief Operating Officer reviews the scope of coverage at each renewal with the Information Security Officer and the CCO, and the CCO confirms that the incident response procedures in this Section and in the Business Continuity Plan are consistent with the policy's notice requirements.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 11. CYBERSECURITY AND INFORMATION SECURITY > 11.8 Identity Theft Prevention
chunks.text: Because Supervised Persons may direct transfers from client accounts under standing letters of authorization, the Firm maintains an identity theft prevention program under Regulation S-ID. Every request to transfer funds to a third party must be verbally confirmed with the client using a telephone number on file, and never a number provided in the request.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 12. PRIVACY OF CLIENT INFORMATION > 12.1 Privacy Notice
chunks.text: The Firm delivers its privacy notice to each client at the start of the relationship. Because the Firm shares nonpublic personal information with nonaffiliated third parties only as permitted by the exceptions in Regulation S-P and has not changed its practices, it relies on the exception from annual delivery of the notice.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 12. PRIVACY OF CLIENT INFORMATION > 12.2 Sharing with Kilnwick Tax Services, LLC
chunks.text: The Firm shares client information with Kilnwick Tax Services, LLC only with the client's written consent, which the client may revoke at any time.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 12. PRIVACY OF CLIENT INFORMATION > 12.3 Safeguards and Disposal
chunks.text: Client information may be stored only on Firm systems. Paper records containing client information are shredded, and electronic media are wiped or destroyed, before disposal.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 13. BOOKS AND RECORDS > 13.1 Required Records
chunks.text: The Firm makes and keeps the books and records required by Rule 204-2 under the Advisers Act, including trade records, client agreements, written communications, advertisements and their support, code of ethics records, and records of the Firm's policies and procedures and their annual review.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 13. BOOKS AND RECORDS > 13.2 Retention Period
chunks.text: Records are retained for five years from the end of the fiscal year during which the last entry was made on the record, the first two years in an office of the Firm. Partnership articles and other organizational documents are retained until at least three years after the termination of the Firm.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 13. BOOKS AND RECORDS > 13.3 Electronic Storage
chunks.text: Records are stored electronically in the Firm's document management system, hosted by Norcastle Managed Services, LLC, in a form that preserves them from alteration and permits prompt retrieval and production to the SEC.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 14. ELECTRONIC COMMUNICATIONS > 14.1 Approved Channels
chunks.text: Business communications may be conducted only through the Firm's email system, the Firm's internal chat platform and the Firm-provided text messaging application installed on Firm-managed mobile devices.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 14. ELECTRONIC COMMUNICATIONS > 14.2 Prohibited Channels
chunks.text: Personal email accounts, personal text messaging and messaging applications not provided by the Firm may not be used for business communications. If a client sends a business communication through an unapproved channel, the Supervised Person must respond only through an approved channel and forward the original message to an approved channel for capture.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 14. ELECTRONIC COMMUNICATIONS > 14.3 Archiving
chunks.text: All business communications on approved channels are captured and retained by Marrowgate Archiving, Inc., the Firm's archiving vendor, in a non-rewriteable, non-erasable format for at least five years. The archive is searchable by Compliance and can be produced to regulators on request.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 14. ELECTRONIC COMMUNICATIONS > 14.4 Surveillance and Review
chunks.text: Compliance reviews lexicon alerts daily and reviews a random sample of not less than 50 messages each week, drawn from all Supervised Persons. Each review and any escalation is documented in the Compliance Platform.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026

chunks.text: Each Supervised Person certifies quarterly through the Compliance Platform that he or she has not used an unapproved channel for business communications or, if he or she has, that each such communication was forwarded for capture.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026

chunks.text: The CCO reviews the adequacy of this Manual and the effectiveness of its implementation at least annually, as required by Rule 206(4)-7. The review considers compliance matters that arose during the year, changes in the Firm's business and changes in applicable law.

chunks.text: The CCO conducts an interim review of any policy affected by a significant compliance event, a material change in the Firm's business or a change in applicable law.

chunks.text: Each new Supervised Person completes compliance training covering this Manual and the Code of Ethics within 30 days of the start of employment.
