chunks.section: Preamble
chunks.text: # Valuation Policy and Procedures **Tennick Arlow Wealth Partners, LLC** **Effective February 10, 2026** > **SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT: FOR BENCHMARK USE ONLY.** This document is fictional. Tennick Arlow Wealth Partners, LLC and all persons, service providers and figures named herein are invented for the purpose of evaluating document-processing systems. It is not an offer to sell securities and does not describe any real entity.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE > 1.1 Purpose
chunks.text: Tennick Arlow Wealth Partners, LLC (the "Firm") relies on the values of client holdings to calculate asset-based advisory fees, to report performance and holdings to clients, and to present composite performance in advertisements. This Policy establishes the procedures by which those values are determined, reviewed and, where necessary, challenged or overridden, so that values are determined fairly and consistently and fees are not calculated on inaccurate values.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE > 1.2 Scope
chunks.text: This Policy applies to every asset held in an account for which the Firm charges a fee or provides performance reporting. The qualified custodian of each account is the official book of record for the account. The Firm does not calculate a net asset value for any pooled vehicle, and nothing in this Policy changes the value shown on a custodian's statement. Where the value the Firm uses for billing or reporting differs from the custodian's value, the Firm's quarterly report to the client identifies the difference.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE > 1.3 Responsibilities
chunks.text: The Operations department, under the Director of Operations, Wendell Ashby, performs the daily pricing controls described in this Policy through the Firm's portfolio accounting system, provided by Tessaline Portfolio Systems, Inc. A Pricing Analyst in the Operations department reviews exception reports each business day. The Valuation Committee oversees the application of this Policy.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. VALUATION COMMITTEE > 2.1 Composition
chunks.text: The Valuation Committee consists of the Chief Financial Officer, who serves as Chair, the Chief Operating Officer, the Director of Operations and a senior portfolio manager designated annually by the Chief Investment Officer. The Chief Compliance Officer attends each meeting as a non-voting member. The Chair of the Committee is currently Graham Oyelaran, Chief Financial Officer.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. VALUATION COMMITTEE > 2.2 Quorum and Voting
chunks.text: A quorum consists of three voting members, one of whom must be the Chair or the Chief Operating Officer. Decisions are made by a majority of the voting members present. A member who has a personal interest in a matter before the Committee, including a personal investment in the asset under review, discloses the interest and does not vote on it.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. VALUATION COMMITTEE > 2.3 Meetings
chunks.text: The Committee meets quarterly, within 15 business days after the end of each calendar quarter, and at other times at the request of any member. At each quarterly meeting the Committee reviews the Override Log, the stale price report, the results of back-testing, every asset valued using Level 3 inputs, and any price challenge that remained unresolved at quarter-end. The Director of Operations prepares the meeting materials, and the minutes are kept by a member of the Operations department.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. VALUATION COMMITTEE > 2.4 Responsibilities
chunks.text: The Committee approves valuation methodologies for asset types not addressed in this Policy, resolves disputed values, approves the valuation of any asset that has no reliable price, and recommends amendments to this Policy to the Management Committee.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. VALUATION COMMITTEE > 2.5 Conflicts of Interest
chunks.text: Because the Firm's fees are calculated on the value of client assets, the Firm has an incentive to use higher values. Portfolio managers and wealth advisors also have an interest in the reported performance of the accounts they manage. The Firm addresses these conflicts by using custodian prices as the primary source, by requiring that overrides be approved outside the portfolio management function, by reporting every override and every Level 3 value to the Valuation Committee, and by subjecting this Policy to the independent review described in Section 8.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. PRICING HIERARCHY AND SOURCES > 3.1 Primary Source
chunks.text: Except for the Level 3 assets described in Section 5, which are valued under that Section, the primary source for the value of every asset is the price reported by the custodian of the account, currently Harlowe Crest Securities, LLC or Brindlemoor Trust Company, N.A. Custodian prices are loaded into the portfolio accounting system each business day.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. PRICING HIERARCHY AND SOURCES > 3.2 Secondary Source and Tolerance Checks
chunks.text: The Firm subscribes to an independent pricing service, Ashcombe Pricing Data, LLC, as its secondary source. Each business day the portfolio accounting system compares the custodian price of each holding with the Ashcombe price and generates an exception when the difference exceeds 0.5% for a listed equity security or exchange-traded fund, or 2% for a fixed income security. The Pricing Analyst investigates each exception the same day and documents the resolution.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. PRICING HIERARCHY AND SOURCES > 3.3 Fair Value Hierarchy
chunks.text: The Firm classifies each asset according to the inputs used to value it. Level 1 assets are valued using unadjusted quoted prices in active markets, such as the closing prices of listed equity securities and exchange-traded funds and the net asset values of open-end mutual funds. Level 2 assets are valued using observable inputs other than Level 1 prices, such as evaluated prices for municipal and corporate bonds derived from comparable trades and yield curves. Level 3 assets are valued using significant unobservable inputs, as described in Section 5.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. PRICING HIERARCHY AND SOURCES > 3.4 Specific Instruments
chunks.text: Listed equity securities and exchange-traded funds are valued at the official closing price on their primary exchange. Open-end mutual funds are valued at their reported net asset value. Fixed income securities are valued at the evaluated bid price reported by the custodian. Listed options, which the Firm writes only as covered calls at a client's request, are valued at the mean of the closing bid and ask prices. Structured notes are valued at the indicative bid provided by the issuer, which the Pricing Analyst compares with the issuer's most recent published valuation. Cash and money market fund balances are valued at their stated balance.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. PRICING HIERARCHY AND SOURCES > 3.5 Held-Away and Accommodation Assets
chunks.text: Assets that a client asks the Firm to include in reporting but that the Firm does not manage, such as employer retirement plan accounts or a closely held business interest, are reported at the value provided by the client or the account provider, are labeled as unmanaged in client reports and are excluded from billable assets. The Firm does not verify those values and does not include them in composite performance.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PRICE CHALLENGES AND OVERRIDES > 4.1 Price Challenges
chunks.text: When the Pricing Analyst or a portfolio manager believes that a custodian price does not reflect the value of an asset, the Operations department submits a price challenge to the custodian, or to Ashcombe where the secondary source appears to be in error, within two business days of identifying the issue. The challenge is supported by evidence such as recent trade prints, dealer quotes or issuer information. Each challenge and its outcome are recorded in the Price Challenge Log.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PRICE CHALLENGES AND OVERRIDES > 4.2 Price Overrides
chunks.text: If a challenge is not resolved before a date on which a value is needed for billing or client reporting, the Firm may use a value other than the primary source price. An override of a primary source price for billing or client reporting must be approved in advance by the Director of Operations. Each override is recorded in the Override Log with the reason for it, the source of the alternative value, the accounts affected and the effect on fees, and is reported to the Valuation Committee at its next meeting. A portfolio manager may request an override but may not approve one.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PRICE CHALLENGES AND OVERRIDES > 4.3 Effect on Billing
chunks.text: Where an override changes a quarter-end value used to calculate fees, the Operations department recalculates the fee for each affected account and retains the calculation with the Override Log. If a value used for billing is later found to have been materially wrong, the Firm credits any overbilled amount on the next invoice.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. LEVEL 3 METHODOLOGY > 5.1 Level 3 Assets
chunks.text: Level 3 assets held in client accounts include interests in private funds recommended by the Firm, shares of non-traded real estate investment trusts and business development companies, private placements and restricted securities for which no observable price exists, and defaulted or suspended securities that no longer trade.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. LEVEL 3 METHODOLOGY > 5.2 Private Funds
chunks.text: Interests in private funds are valued at the most recent net asset value reported by the fund's administrator or general partner, adjusted for capital contributions and distributions made after the date of that net asset value. When the custodian reports a value for a private fund interest, the Operations department compares it with the value determined under this Section and refers any difference of more than 1% to the Director of Operations.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. LEVEL 3 METHODOLOGY > 5.3 Non-Traded Vehicles
chunks.text: Shares of non-traded real estate investment trusts and business development companies are valued at the most recent estimated per-share value published by the sponsor. If the sponsor has suspended redemptions, the Valuation Committee considers whether a discount to the published value is appropriate.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. LEVEL 3 METHODOLOGY > 5.4 Restricted and Defaulted Securities
chunks.text: Restricted securities of an issuer that also has freely traded securities are valued at the price of the freely traded securities less a discount that reflects the restriction's remaining term, as approved by the Valuation Committee. Defaulted or suspended securities for which no reliable price is available are valued at zero once the Valuation Committee determines that recovery is unlikely.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. LEVEL 3 METHODOLOGY > 5.5 Documentation
chunks.text: For each Level 3 asset, the Operations department maintains a valuation file containing the source documents, the calculation and the approval of the Valuation Committee where one is required. When a fund administrator or sponsor revises a previously reported value, the Operations department records the revision, determines whether any fee or client report was affected, and reports the revision to the Valuation Committee at its next meeting.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. STALE PRICE MONITORING > 6.1 Stale Price Thresholds
chunks.text: The portfolio accounting system flags as stale a listed equity security or exchange-traded fund whose price has not changed for five consecutive business days, a fixed income security whose price has not changed for ten consecutive business days, and a private fund whose most recent reported net asset value is dated more than 120 days before the valuation date.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. STALE PRICE MONITORING > 6.2 Review and Escalation
chunks.text: The Pricing Analyst reviews the stale price report each business day and investigates each flagged asset. A stale price that is not resolved within five business days is escalated to the Director of Operations, and every stale price outstanding at quarter-end is reported to the Valuation Committee.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. BACK-TESTING > 7.1 Procedure
chunks.text: Each quarter the Operations department compares each Level 3 value and each overridden price used in the preceding quarter with the next observable transaction price or subsequently reported net asset value for the same asset. Any variance greater than 5% is investigated, and the Director of Operations documents its cause and whether the methodology should be changed. The results are presented to the Valuation Committee at its next quarterly meeting.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. INDEPENDENT REVIEW > 8.1 Annual Compliance Review
chunks.text: The Chief Compliance Officer reviews the adequacy of this Policy and the effectiveness of its implementation annually as part of the Firm's annual compliance review.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. INDEPENDENT REVIEW > 8.2 External Review
chunks.text: Every two years, an independent valuation firm, currently Wraxall Dunmore Advisory, LLC, reviews this Policy and tests a sample of Level 3 valuations and price overrides. The external reviewer's report is delivered to the Valuation Committee and the Management Committee, and the Chief Compliance Officer tracks each recommendation to resolution.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. RECORDKEEPING AND AMENDMENTS > 9.1 Records
chunks.text: The Operations department retains the Price Challenge Log, the Override Log, stale price reports, back-testing results, Level 3 valuation files and Valuation Committee minutes for at least five years.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. RECORDKEEPING AND AMENDMENTS > 9.2 Amendments
chunks.text: Amendments to this Policy are approved by the Management Committee on the recommendation of the Valuation Committee.

Tennick Arlow Wealth Partners, LLC and all persons, service providers and figures named herein are invented for the purpose of evaluating document-processing systems. chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. PURPOSE, SCOPE AND ASSUMPTIONS > 1.1 Purpose
chunks.text: This Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan (the "Plan") describes how Tennick Arlow Wealth Partners, LLC (the "Firm") will continue to meet its obligations to clients during and after a Significant Business Disruption. As a fiduciary, the Firm must be able to protect client information, maintain access to client accounts and continue to manage client portfolios when its offices, systems, personnel or vendors are unavailable.

chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. PURPOSE, SCOPE AND ASSUMPTIONS > 1.2 Scope
chunks.text: The Plan covers the Firm's three offices, in Richmond, Virginia (the principal office), Charlottesville, Virginia and Raleigh, North Carolina, all Supervised Persons, and the systems and vendors listed in Section 3 and Section 5. Client assets are held by unaffiliated qualified custodians, which maintain their own business continuity plans. A disruption at the Firm does not prevent clients from contacting their custodian directly to obtain account information or to request withdrawals.

chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. PURPOSE, SCOPE AND ASSUMPTIONS > 1.3 Significant Business Disruption
chunks.text: A Significant Business Disruption is any event that prevents the Firm from operating one or more offices or critical systems in the normal course, including loss of an office through fire, flood or utility failure, a regional disaster, a public health emergency, a cybersecurity incident, the loss of a critical vendor, or the unavailability of key personnel.

chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. PLAN OWNERSHIP AND GOVERNANCE > 2.1 Plan Owner
chunks.text: Harriet Solberg, Chief Operating Officer, is the owner of this Plan. The Plan Owner is responsible for maintaining the Plan, for declaring a Significant Business Disruption and for directing the Firm's response. Owen Stahlberg, Director of Technology, serves as BCP Coordinator and is responsible for the technical recovery procedures, for vendor recovery arrangements and for organizing the tests described in Section 7.

chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. PLAN OWNERSHIP AND GOVERNANCE > 2.2 Approval and Review
chunks.text: The Management Committee approves the Plan and each material amendment. The Plan Owner reviews the Plan at least annually, after each activation and after each test, and whenever the Firm opens an office, changes a critical vendor or adopts a new critical system. The Chief Compliance Officer reviews the Plan as part of the annual compliance review.

chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. PLAN OWNERSHIP AND GOVERNANCE > 2.3 Declaration and Delegation of Authority
chunks.text: The Plan Owner declares a Significant Business Disruption and activates the Plan. If the Plan Owner is unavailable, the Chief Financial Officer may declare a Significant Business Disruption and exercise the Plan Owner's authority under the Plan, and if both are unavailable, the Managing Partner may do so.

chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. RECOVERY OBJECTIVES > 3.1 Recovery Time Objectives
chunks.text: The Firm classifies its systems in three tiers according to their importance to clients. Tier 1 systems are the order management and trading system, access to the custodians' advisor platforms, the portfolio accounting system and the Firm's email and telephone systems. The recovery time objective for Tier 1 systems is 24 hours from the declaration of a Significant Business Disruption. Tier 2 systems are the client relationship management system, the financial planning software, the document management system and the billing module of the portfolio accounting system; their recovery time objective is 48 hours. Tier 3 systems are all other systems, including the public website and internal collaboration tools; their recovery time objective is five business days.

chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. RECOVERY OBJECTIVES > 3.2 Manual Workarounds
chunks.text: Until a Tier 1 system is recovered, traders may place orders directly through the custodians' advisor platforms or by telephone to the custodians' trading desks, and portfolio managers may use custodian holdings reports in place of the portfolio accounting system. Manual orders are logged and reconciled once the order management system is restored.

chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. ALTERNATE SITES AND REMOTE WORK > 4.1 Alternate Sites
chunks.text: If the Richmond office is unavailable, the Charlottesville office serves as the primary alternate site for trading, operations and client service. If both the Richmond and Charlottesville offices are unavailable, the Raleigh office serves as the secondary alternate site. If the Charlottesville or Raleigh office is unavailable, its personnel work from the Richmond office or remotely. Each office maintains workstations, network connections and printers configured for use by personnel from the other offices.

chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. ALTERNATE SITES AND REMOTE WORK > 4.2 Remote Work
chunks.text: Every Supervised Person is issued a Firm-managed laptop and may work remotely through the Firm's secure remote access service, which requires multi-factor authentication. All Tier 1 and Tier 2 systems are accessible remotely. Traders keep Firm-managed mobile devices with approved access to the custodians' advisor platforms.

chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. ALTERNATE SITES AND REMOTE WORK > 4.3 Physical Records
chunks.text: The Firm keeps few physical records. Original documents that must be kept in paper form, such as executed trust instruments delivered by clients, are scanned into the document management system on receipt and the originals are stored in fire-resistant cabinets in the Richmond office.

chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. CRITICAL VENDORS > 5.1 Vendor Oversight
chunks.text: The Plan Owner and the BCP Coordinator maintain a list of critical vendors, obtain each vendor's business continuity summary and, where available, its most recent independent controls report, and review them annually as part of the vendor due diligence required by the Compliance Manual.

chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. CRITICAL VENDORS > 5.2 Critical Vendor List
chunks.text: | Vendor | Service | |---|---| | Harlowe Crest Securities, LLC | Custody, execution and advisor platform | | Brindlemoor Trust Company, N.A. | Custody of trust and certain retirement accounts | | Tessaline Portfolio Systems, Inc. | Portfolio accounting, performance reporting and billing | | Norcastle Managed Services, LLC | Managed IT services, cloud hosting and data backup | | Marrowgate Archiving, Inc. | Archiving of electronic communications | | Ashcombe Pricing Data, LLC | Secondary pricing source | | Veridane Proxy Services, Inc. | Proxy research, vote execution and records | | Kettleby Compliance Systems, Inc. | Compliance platform | For each critical vendor, the BCP Coordinator maintains primary and after-hours contacts and the vendor's commitments for restoring service to the Firm.

chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. DATA BACKUP AND RECOVERY > 6.1 Backup Frequency
chunks.text: Norcastle performs incremental backups of the Firm's file server and document management system every four hours between 6:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m. Eastern time on business days, and a full backup every night. Cloud applications provided by Tessaline and the Firm's client relationship management provider are backed up by those providers under their own controls, which the BCP Coordinator reviews annually.

chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. DATA BACKUP AND RECOVERY > 6.2 Storage Location and Retention
chunks.text: Backup copies are replicated to Norcastle's secondary data center in Columbus, Ohio, more than 300 miles from each Firm office. Nightly backups are held in immutable storage for 35 days, and a monthly full backup is retained for 12 months.

chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. DATA BACKUP AND RECOVERY > 6.3 Restoration Testing
chunks.text: Norcastle restores a sample of files and one full system image from backup each quarter. The BCP Coordinator reviews the results and records any failure and its remediation.

chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. TESTING AND TRAINING > 7.1 Testing Frequency and Most Recent Test
chunks.text: The Plan is tested at least annually. The most recent full test of the Plan was conducted on October 22, 2025. It combined a tabletop exercise, based on a scenario in which the Richmond office was closed by a regional power outage, with a live exercise in which the trading desk operated from the Charlottesville office and all other personnel worked remotely for a full business day. The results were reported to the Management Committee on November 12, 2025. The next full test is scheduled for October 2026.

chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. TESTING AND TRAINING > 7.2 Follow-Up
chunks.text: The BCP Coordinator records each issue identified in a test, assigns an owner and a completion date, and reports open items to the Plan Owner monthly until they are resolved.

chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. TESTING AND TRAINING > 7.3 Training
chunks.text: Each Supervised Person receives training on the Plan when joining the Firm and annually, including the use of remote access, the communication procedures in Section 8 and his or her role during a Significant Business Disruption.

chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. COMMUNICATION TREE > 8.1 Activation
chunks.text: When the Plan is activated, the Plan Owner, or the person exercising the Plan Owner's authority under Section 2.3, sends an alert to all Supervised Persons through the Firm's mass notification service by text message, voice call and email. Each Supervised Person must acknowledge the alert within 60 minutes.

chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. COMMUNICATION TREE > 8.2 Internal Tree
chunks.text: The Plan Owner contacts the other members of the Management Committee, the Chief Compliance Officer, the BCP Coordinator, the Head of Trading, and the Managing Directors of the Charlottesville and Raleigh offices, Everett Linwood and Camille Dubrow. Each of them contacts the personnel who report to them and confirms their status and location. Any Supervised Person who has not been reached within two hours is reported to the Plan Owner, who directs further efforts to make contact.

chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. COMMUNICATION TREE > 8.3 External Communications
chunks.text: The Firm informs clients of a Significant Business Disruption through a notice on its website and by email, and wealth advisors contact affected households directly by telephone where a disruption is expected to last more than one business day. The Head of Trading and the BCP Coordinator notify the custodians and critical vendors. The Chief Compliance Officer determines whether any notice to a regulator is required. Only the Managing Partner, or a person she designates, may speak to the media.

chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. PANDEMIC AND PUBLIC HEALTH EVENTS > 9.1 Response
chunks.text: During a pandemic or other public health emergency, the Plan Owner may direct some or all personnel to work remotely, may divide the trading and operations teams between the Richmond and Charlottesville offices so that no single exposure disables either function, and may suspend in-person client meetings. Each critical function has at least one cross-trained backup, and the Plan Owner reviews backup coverage when absences increase. Personnel who are ill are expected to remain at home and notify their supervisor.

chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 10. CYBER INCIDENT RESPONSE > 10.1 Incident Response Team
chunks.text: The Incident Response Team is led by the Information Security Officer, Owen Stahlberg, and includes the Chief Operating Officer, the Chief Compliance Officer and the Firm's outside counsel, Garrow Whitcombe LLP. The Information Security Officer may engage a forensic investigation firm through counsel, including a firm approved under the Firm's cyber liability insurance policy.

chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 10. CYBER INCIDENT RESPONSE > 10.2 Response Phases
chunks.text: The Incident Response Team identifies and contains the incident, preserves evidence, eradicates the cause and restores affected systems from clean backups. Where client account credentials or client information may have been compromised, the Team notifies the custodians immediately so that they can place alerts on the affected accounts. The Chief Compliance Officer is responsible for notifications to affected individuals and regulators under the Compliance Manual.

chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 10. CYBER INCIDENT RESPONSE > 10.3 Ransomware
chunks.text: No ransom or extortion payment may be made without the approval of the Management Committee after consultation with outside counsel and law enforcement. The Firm's priority in a ransomware event is to restore systems from backups held in immutable storage.

chunks.label: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan, dated May 4, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 11. PLAN MAINTENANCE > 11.1 Contact Lists and Records
chunks.text: The BCP Coordinator updates personnel and vendor contact lists quarterly and after any change in personnel. Copies of the Plan and the contact lists are kept in the document management system, on each Management Committee member's Firm-managed mobile device and in printed form at each office.

chunks.text: # Schedule of Advisory Fees **Tennick Arlow Wealth Partners, LLC** **Effective April 1, 2026** > **SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT: FOR BENCHMARK USE ONLY.** This document is fictional. Tennick Arlow Wealth Partners, LLC and all persons, service providers and figures named herein are invented for the purpose of evaluating document-processing systems. chunks.label: Schedule of Advisory Fees, dated April 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. SCOPE AND DEFINITIONS > 1.1 Scope
chunks.text: This Schedule forms part of each Investment Advisory Agreement between Tennick Arlow Wealth Partners, LLC (the "Firm") and its clients. If a client's signed Investment Advisory Agreement specifies a different fee, the Agreement controls.

chunks.label: Schedule of Advisory Fees, dated April 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. SCOPE AND DEFINITIONS > 1.2 Definitions
chunks.text: "Billable Assets" means all assets in accounts managed by the Firm, including cash and cash equivalents, other than assets the Firm reports on but does not manage. "Billing Value" means the value of Billable Assets as reported by the custodian or, for assets the custodian does not price and for Level 3 assets such as private fund interests, as determined under the Firm's Valuation Policy, including accrued interest. "Household" has the meaning given in Section 2.2.

chunks.label: Schedule of Advisory Fees, dated April 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. WEALTH MANAGEMENT FEE > 2.1 Standard Tiered Schedule
chunks.text: | Household Billable Assets | Annual rate | |---|---| | First $1,000,000 | 1.00% | | Next $2,000,000 (over $1,000,000 up to $3,000,000) | 0.80% | | Next $2,000,000 (over $3,000,000 up to $5,000,000) | 0.65% | | Next $5,000,000 (over $5,000,000 up to $10,000,000) | 0.50% | | Over $10,000,000 | 0.35% | Each rate applies only to the Billable Assets within its tier. The fee includes portfolio management, financial planning and the coordination services described in the Firm's Form ADV Part 2A.

chunks.label: Schedule of Advisory Fees, dated April 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. WEALTH MANAGEMENT FEE > 2.2 Household Aggregation
chunks.text: A Household consists of the client, the client's spouse or domestic partner, their dependent children, and trusts, foundations and entities of which one or more of them is the grantor, primary beneficiary or controlling owner. The Billable Assets of all accounts in a Household are aggregated to determine the applicable tiers, and the resulting fee is allocated among the accounts in proportion to their Billing Values unless the client directs otherwise.

chunks.label: Schedule of Advisory Fees, dated April 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. WEALTH MANAGEMENT FEE > 2.3 Minimum Relationship and Minimum Fee
chunks.text: The minimum household relationship for new clients is $1,000,000 of Billable Assets, and the minimum annual fee is $10,000, billed as $2,500 per quarter. Households that became clients before July 1, 2025 remain subject to the $750,000 minimum relationship in effect when they engaged the Firm. The Managing Partner may waive or reduce either minimum in writing.

chunks.label: Schedule of Advisory Fees, dated April 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. FIXED INCOME MANDATES > 3.1 Schedule
chunks.text: Standalone Tax-Managed Municipal and Taxable Fixed Income portfolios are charged 0.40% annually on the first $5,000,000 and 0.30% on Billable Assets above $5,000,000. The minimum Fixed Income Mandate is $2,000,000.

chunks.label: Schedule of Advisory Fees, dated April 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. FIXED INCOME MANDATES > 3.2 No Aggregation
chunks.text: Fixed Income Mandate assets are billed under Section 3.1 only and are not included in the Household total used to apply Section 2.1.

chunks.label: Schedule of Advisory Fees, dated April 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. FINANCIAL PLANNING AND CONSULTING > 4.1 Standalone Planning
chunks.text: Standalone financial planning engagements are charged a fixed fee between $5,000 and $25,000, stated in the engagement letter. Half of the fee is due on signing and the balance on delivery of the written plan.

chunks.label: Schedule of Advisory Fees, dated April 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. FINANCIAL PLANNING AND CONSULTING > 4.2 Hourly Consulting
chunks.text: Hourly consulting is charged at $400 per hour, billed monthly in arrears.

chunks.label: Schedule of Advisory Fees, dated April 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. BILLING > 5.1 Frequency and Basis
chunks.text: Wealth management and Fixed Income Mandate fees are billed quarterly in advance, based on the Billing Value of each account on the last business day of the preceding calendar quarter. The quarterly fee is one quarter of the annual fee calculated under Section 2 or Section 3.

chunks.label: Schedule of Advisory Fees, dated April 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. BILLING > 5.2 Payment
chunks.text: Unless the client elects to be invoiced, fees are deducted from the account designated by the client under the authority granted in the Investment Advisory Agreement. Invoiced fees are payable within 30 days of the invoice date.

chunks.label: Schedule of Advisory Fees, dated April 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. BILLING > 5.3 Contributions and Withdrawals
chunks.text: A contribution or withdrawal of $100,000 or more in a single transaction during a quarter results in a pro rata charge or credit, based on the number of days remaining in the quarter, on the next quarterly invoice. Smaller contributions and withdrawals are not adjusted.

chunks.label: Schedule of Advisory Fees, dated April 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. BILLING > 5.4 New Accounts
chunks.text: The fee for the first partial quarter is calculated on the Billing Value at the date of funding, prorated for the days remaining in the quarter, and billed with the first full quarter.

chunks.label: Schedule of Advisory Fees, dated April 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. TERMINATION AND REFUNDS > 6.1 Notice
chunks.text: Either party may terminate the Investment Advisory Agreement upon 30 days' written notice to the other party.

chunks.label: Schedule of Advisory Fees, dated April 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. TERMINATION AND REFUNDS > 6.2 Refund of Prepaid Fees
chunks.text: On termination, the unearned portion of the prepaid fee is refunded pro rata based on the number of days remaining in the quarter after the effective date of termination. Refunds are paid within 15 business days of the effective date of termination. No termination fee is charged by the Firm.

chunks.label: Schedule of Advisory Fees, dated April 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. TERMINATION AND REFUNDS > 6.3 Five-Business-Day Cancellation
chunks.text: A client who terminates within five business days of signing the Investment Advisory Agreement receives a full refund of any fees paid.

chunks.label: Schedule of Advisory Fees, dated April 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. FEES NOT INCLUDED > 7.1 Third-Party Costs
chunks.text: The fees in this Schedule do not include custodian charges, transaction charges, dealer markups, wire and transfer fees, or the management fees and expenses of mutual funds, exchange-traded funds and private funds, all of which are borne by the client.

chunks.label: Memorandum: Amendments to Firm Policies and Procedures, dated August 17, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. PURPOSE AND EFFECT > SECTION 1. PURPOSE AND EFFECT
chunks.text: On August 12, 2026, the Management Committee approved the amendments described in this memorandum. Each amendment identifies the document and section it amends and supersedes the provision it identifies. The affected documents are the Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual (Version 7.0, effective January 15, 2026), the Valuation Policy and Procedures (effective February 10, 2026), the Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan (Version 5.2, revised May 4, 2026), the Schedule of Advisory Fees (effective April 1, 2026) and the Form ADV Part 2A brochure dated March 27, 2026. The affected documents have not yet been reissued and continue to show the prior provisions. Where this memorandum conflicts with an earlier document, this memorandum controls. Unless a section below states otherwise, each amendment is effective on the date of this memorandum.

chunks.label: Memorandum: Amendments to Firm Policies and Procedures, dated August 17, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. PERSONAL TRADING: MINIMUM HOLDING PERIOD > SECTION 2. PERSONAL TRADING: MINIMUM HOLDING PERIOD
chunks.text: **Amends:** Compliance Manual, Section 4.5 (Minimum Holding Period). The minimum holding period for Reportable Securities acquired in a Covered Account is increased from 30 calendar days to 60 calendar days. This change supersedes the 30-day period stated in Section 4.5 of the Compliance Manual. The 60-day period applies to every Reportable Security acquired on or after the date of this memorandum; securities acquired before that date remain subject to the 30-day period. The disgorgement and hardship exception provisions of Section 4.5 are unchanged. Compliance's review of 2025 personal trading identified repeated short-term trading in securities also held in the Core Equity strategy, and the Management Committee concluded that a longer holding period better separates personal trading from model activity.

chunks.label: Memorandum: Amendments to Firm Policies and Procedures, dated August 17, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. VALUATION: APPROVAL OF PRICE OVERRIDES > SECTION 3. VALUATION: APPROVAL OF PRICE OVERRIDES
chunks.text: **Amends:** Valuation Policy, Section 4.2 (Price Overrides). Any override of a primary source price used for billing or client reporting must now be approved in writing by both the Chief Financial Officer and the Chief Compliance Officer before it is applied. This change supersedes the requirement in Section 4.2 of the Valuation Policy that overrides be approved in advance by the Director of Operations. The Director of Operations continues to prepare each override request and to maintain the Override Log, and overrides continue to be reported to the Valuation Committee at its next meeting. Because the Operations department also calculates client fees, the Management Committee concluded that override approval should sit with officers who do not perform the fee calculation.

chunks.label: Memorandum: Amendments to Firm Policies and Procedures, dated August 17, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. BUSINESS CONTINUITY: TIER 1 RECOVERY TIME OBJECTIVE > SECTION 4. BUSINESS CONTINUITY: TIER 1 RECOVERY TIME OBJECTIVE
chunks.text: **Amends:** Business Continuity Plan, Section 3.1 (Recovery Time Objectives). The recovery time objective for Tier 1 systems is shortened from 24 hours to 8 hours from the declaration of a Significant Business Disruption. This change supersedes the 24-hour objective stated in Section 3.1 of the Business Continuity Plan. The change is supported by the amendment to the Firm's agreement with Norcastle Managed Services, LLC executed on August 5, 2026, under which Norcastle maintains a warm standby environment for the order management system. The recovery time objectives for Tier 2 and Tier 3 systems are unchanged.

chunks.label: Memorandum: Amendments to Firm Policies and Procedures, dated August 17, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. FEE SCHEDULE: TOP BREAKPOINT > SECTION 5. FEE SCHEDULE: TOP BREAKPOINT

The Chief Compliance Officer will file an other-than-annual amendment to the brochure, and affected clients will be notified by letter.

chunks.text: **Amends:** Compliance Manual, Section 14.3 (Archiving), and Business Continuity Plan, Section 5.2 (Critical Vendor List).
